title: Introduction to Programming — Building with Logic and Order: Unit Quiz

questions.question: What is sequential execution in programming?
options: Running multiple instructions at the same time
Processing instructions one at a time from top to bottom
Skipping instructions that are not needed
Running instructions in random order
questions.explanation: Sequential execution means the computer processes instructions one at a time, in order from top to bottom. Each instruction is completed before the next one begins.

questions.question: What is a variable in programming?
options: A type of loop that repeats code
A named container that stores a piece of information
A command that displays text on screen
A type of error in code
questions.explanation: A variable is a named container that stores data in the computer's memory. It has a name (like a label) and a value (the stored information).

questions.question: What is a Boolean value?
options: A decimal number
A long text string
A value that is either true or false
A variable that cannot be changed
questions.explanation: A Boolean value can only be one of two things: true or false. Boolean logic is the foundation of all computer decision-making.

questions.question: What is the difference between a 'for loop' and a 'while loop'?
options: A for loop is faster than a while loop
A for loop repeats a set number of times; a while loop repeats as long as a condition is true
A while loop can only run once; a for loop runs multiple times
There is no difference between them
questions.explanation: A for loop repeats a predetermined number of times, while a while loop continues repeating as long as its condition remains true.

questions.question: What is a function in programming?
options: A type of variable that stores numbers
An error message from the computer
A named block of code that performs a specific task
A command that stops a program
questions.explanation: A function is a named, reusable block of code that performs a specific task. Functions help organize code and prevent repetition.

questions.question: What is an algorithm?
options: A type of programming language
A precise, step-by-step procedure for solving a problem
A computer hardware component
A type of variable that stores text
questions.explanation: An algorithm is a precise, step-by-step procedure for solving a problem or completing a task. Algorithms must be clear enough for a computer to follow.

questions.question: What does 'decomposition' mean in computational thinking?
options: Deleting old code that is no longer needed
Breaking a large problem into smaller, manageable parts
Converting code from one language to another
Finding and fixing bugs in a program
questions.explanation: Decomposition means breaking a complex problem into smaller, more manageable parts. Each smaller part can then be solved individually.

questions.question: Why is it wrong to copy someone else's code without giving credit?
options: Because the code will not work if copied
Because it violates copyright and is a form of intellectual theft
Because copied code always contains viruses
Because computers can detect copied code
questions.explanation: Copying code without credit violates intellectual property rights and is a form of theft. The Bible commands us not to steal (Exodus 20:15), and this principle applies to ideas and creative works as well as physical property.
